claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar alloy.
As-sintered equimolar WTaTiVZr has a single-phase BCC structure.
WTaTiVZr exhibits lattice distortion relative to commercially processed high-purity tungsten.
Pure tungsten is used as a plasma-facing material and as a reference material in nuclear-reactor-related studies.
Pure tungsten has a high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature and associated limitations in ductility.
The elevated-temperature nano-indentation creep response of TaTiVWZr has previously been compared with pure tungsten.
Local lattice distortions and heterogeneous micro-stresses are inherent to WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr facilitates dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr activates additional slip systems.
Random substitution of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr creates a distorted lattice.
The distorted lattice lowers the activation energy for dislocation movement.
Pure tungsten has a more ordered structure and a higher Peierls barrier than WTaTiVZr.
Easier dislocation motion and activation of multiple slip systems increase plastic strain and crack-propagation energy absorption.
At 1000–1200 °C, WTaTiVZr will have a lower yield stress than pure tungsten under identical testing conditions.
At 1000–1200 °C, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
At 1000–1200 °C, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will show greater dislocation activity and slip-system activation than pure tungsten during high-temperature deformation.
The hypothesized benefit applies primarily at temperatures where dislocation mobility is thermally activated and may be diminished at lower temperatures.
Testing without irradiation isolates lattice-distortion and dislocation-mechanics effects.
A controlled comparison will use similarly processed WTaTiVZr and pure-tungsten samples tested at 1000–1200 °C by tensile testing, TEM, and fractography.

contradictions.description: The initial state is asserted to be single-phase BCC, while the uncertainty field allows potential influences from minor secondary phases without clarifying whether such phases are present or excluded in the proposed samples.
